project.name: cefr-recommendation-classifier
project.description: Predicts the best study recommendation label from a completed CEFR diagnostic result while leaving grading and study-content generation in application code.

foundation_meaning.title: Rebuild Core Meaning
foundation_meaning.summaryTemplate: Your {estimatedLevel} result shows that {weakestSkill} questions are still dragging down the rest of the test. Rebuild high-frequency word knowledge first, then return to mixed practice.
foundation_meaning.rationaleTemplate: Because {weakestSkill} is currently weaker than {strongestSkill}, stronger meaning control should lift accuracy across every other question type.
techniques: Review 15 high-frequency words per day with synonym, antonym, and one sentence.
Use two-pass correction: choose an answer, then explain why the other options are wrong.
Group missed words into word families instead of memorizing isolated items.

context_clues_boost.title: Strengthen Context Clues
context_clues_boost.summaryTemplate: Your {estimatedLevel} band is forming, but sentence-context questions are lowering your final score. Train yourself to read clue words before locking in an option.
context_clues_boost.rationaleTemplate: Your strongest work is in {strongestSkill}, so the next gain comes from turning sentence clues into faster decisions when {weakestSkill} items appear.
books: English Vocabulary in Use Pre-intermediate and Intermediate
courses: British Council reading and context practice
techniques: Underline tense, tone, and connector words before answering.
Predict the missing word type first, then compare answer choices.
Practice sentence-completion sets in short timed batches of five.

collocation_pattern_builder.title: Build Collocation Patterns
collocation_pattern_builder.summaryTemplate: You can already recognize many target words, but natural word partnerships are holding back your {estimatedLevel} progress. Shift practice toward phrases instead of single words.
collocation_pattern_builder.rationaleTemplate: Since {weakestSkill} is the weakest area and {strongestSkill} is already steadier, phrase-level repetition should make your answers sound more natural and precise.
books: Oxford Collocations Dictionary for Students of English
courses: BBC Learning English phrase and collocation lessons
British Council speaking and vocabulary practice
techniques: Collect missed answers as two-word or three-word chunks, not single terms.
Build a weekly notebook of common verb-noun and adjective-noun pairs.
Repeat collocation drills aloud so the pattern becomes automatic.

word_form_control.title: Tighten Word Form Control
word_form_control.summaryTemplate: Your score suggests the main drag is word-form control. To move beyond {estimatedLevel}, practice prefixes, suffixes, and part-of-speech shifts inside full sentences.
word_form_control.rationaleTemplate: You already show better control in {strongestSkill}, so the fastest improvement comes from reducing errors in {weakestSkill} when grammar and vocabulary interact.
books: Check Your Vocabulary for English Language Exams
courses: Perfect English Grammar word formation practice
British Council grammar and vocabulary lessons
techniques: Create word-family tables with noun, verb, adjective, and adverb forms.
Practice filling blanks only after deciding which part of speech is required.
Review prefixes and suffixes in small themed sets three times per week.

b1_bridge_builder.title: Bridge Toward B1 Stability
b1_bridge_builder.summaryTemplate: Your result is close to stable B1 work. The best next step is mixed review that connects meaning, context, collocation, and form instead of isolating one skill only.
b1_bridge_builder.rationaleTemplate: Because your accuracy is more balanced overall, a structured mixed routine will turn partial control into a steadier {estimatedLevel}-to-B1 transition.
books: English Vocabulary in Use Pre-intermediate and Intermediate
courses: British Council B1 vocabulary and reading practice
techniques: Rotate through four mini-sets: meaning, context, collocation, and word form.
Review wrong answers in one notebook with a short rule under each item.
Finish each study block with five timed mixed questions.

b2_precision_push.title: Push Toward B2 Precision
b2_precision_push.summaryTemplate: You are already moving into stronger territory. To push toward B2, focus on precision: nuanced meaning, natural collocation, and accurate choices under time pressure.
b2_precision_push.rationaleTemplate: Your overall profile is solid enough that the next gains come from sharpening precision, especially when {weakestSkill} appears inside harder mixed items.
courses: BBC Learning English advanced vocabulary lessons
techniques: Track near-synonyms and note when each one sounds more natural.
Practice mixed timed sets of ten questions and review only the borderline choices.
Write one new sentence for every missed item to lock in nuance and register.
